implementation_notes: #[automock] generates a MockTrait from the trait definition, and the test configures one expectation per method - mock.expect_now().times(1).returning(|| epoch), return_const(value), return_once(value) for non-Clone answers, with(with(predicate)) for argument matching. Every expectation must carry a return value (or the nightly default-value support must be enabled), so the generated Expectation builder is the configuration interface and unexpected or missing calls panic. That makes the crate the standard route to a reusable configurable double in Rust, where trait objects or generics provide the substitution seam.
pitfalls: Generics on mocked methods must be 'static and cannot carry lifetime parameters, so traits with borrowed return values need mock! or a hand-written fake instead.
Expectations are consumed in order and panic on violation, so a mock reused across assertions in one test must be re-configured deliberately rather than reused as a plain stub.
The generated mock type lives beside the trait, so mocking a trait from another crate requires the automock/external-trait features to be enabled or a wrapper trait.

variants.name: Hand-written fake struct with RefCell-configured answers
variants.idiom_name: hand-written fake struct implementing the trait with RefCell-configured responses
variants.implementation_notes: A fake struct implements the trait and keeps its canned answers in fields - a VecDeque of successive responses, a boxed closure, or a recorded-call log - mutated through RefCell because trait methods take &self; that is the hand-built configuration interface, and it needs no proc-macro dependency, works in integration tests and across crates, and keeps the compiler checking the full trait. Prefer it for small traits, for fakes that must return borrowed data, and when the double should also implement real behaviour such as an in-memory repository.
pitfalls: RefCell enforces borrows at runtime: a configured closure that re-enters the same fake panics with already-borrowed/cannot-borrow errors instead of failing a test assertion.
A fake shared behind Arc needs interior mutability that is also Sync (Mutex/RwLock) once tests run in parallel threads, or the borrow panics become data races of a different kind.
Fake structs are not checked against the real implementation's behaviour, so a fake that returns impossible values keeps the test green while the production path is broken.
